correctness.rationale: Independently verified without needing the cited sharp cutoff for cycles. After the first move on cycles of size at least 16, use a private cyclic orientation to maintain that each gap between consecutive pebbled sites is either equal on the two cycles or is at least 2^(r+1) on each, where r rounds remain. A repeat is matched exactly; a new vertex splits a gap. Equal gaps may be split identically, and for a large gap one matches a side shorter than 2^r if there is one, or splits into two gaps of at least 2^r. With no moves left the gap-1 incidences and equality are preserved, including the two-pebble wraparound case. Coordinatewise replies preserve equality and Cartesian adjacency in the products, so 105 unordered pairs with dimensions 3 through 16 suffice. The independent computation fixes the first move using transitivity and uses three disjoint vertex bitsets per pebble (equal, adjacent, otherwise). It records all nonempty intersections for fourth-move patterns, retaining sets of rooted extension types at ranks up the game tree without multiplicities. This is precisely the back-and-forth criterion, not a heuristic invariant. It found the asserted 19-class partition and largest least representative (64, 8, 8), and also distinguished C8 from C11. Any noncanonical smaller representative would truncate to one no larger, so sharpness holds throughout the family.
residual_risks: The bound is only among unmarked Cartesian products of two simple cycles of length at least three, not other toroidal graphs or logical signatures.
